utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Roberts. I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Are you ready Mr. Misetic to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honours. One housekeeping matter. We left yesterday with the exhibit 1D41-0043 and I would like to tender that into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection. Of course, this -- I'm not quite sure what the documents are from although some other documents I think later reveal that it was the Croatian authorities who seized these documents or -- but some of them are not signed. I think this specific one hasn't been signed so there is some issue about reliability, but we don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what you actually say is be careful but we do not object. I mean, we're always careful, Mr. Waespi. If there's a real issue about not being signed, then, of course, if there are no objections we will admit and then we will see what weight to give it. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D702.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D702 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning again, Mr. Roberts.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. Could I just one point of clarification. I know it is it not appropriate, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it depends what you seek to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please advise me, Your Honour. I'm in your hands. In regard to the file of articles which I was given by Defence counsel I was invited to review these and I did last night, and I've made my responses and I can do them orally but I have also prepared a very small brief and I've gone through every single article in the file and I have colour coded them with my quotations and those of other UN senior spokespersons and officials. I would like to ask, if I can, to have this file entered as my response with the memo in front of it which I can explain or would like to explain at the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My proposal, Your Honour, would be that Mr. Waespi and I during the next break take a look at the binder so that I could at least see what it is and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- ask questions about it in the next portion if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Or tender --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Or -- right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, there is one thing, Mr. Misetic, you asked the question. You asked the witness to do something and to tell us what he found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So finally, under those circumstances, I would say, whether it is in written form or in oral form, the Chamber is entitled to receive a response to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I just would like to see, what he said, some sort of writing, analysis or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. What we'll do, Mr. Roberts, is that if you would give a copy of your written response, so to say, to the parties, they have a look at it and then they will see whether it is a format in which the Chamber could receive your answers, and if not, then Mr. Misetic will give you an opportunity to answer the question he yesterday put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand. I would like a chance to respond orally as well, but I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, both I leave it to some extent in Mr. Misetic's hands. He is limited in his time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have clearly answered the question, then I take it, Mr. Misetic, you'll give an opportunity to Mr. Roberts --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to add whatever he wants to add --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to his written answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, if I could call up 1D41-0401. This is a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, this is a sort clip of the press conference held in the ARSK headquarters with General Forand and yourself on the 4th of August at around noon. This is the press conference that you reference in your statement. Again, it is only a short portion of it; it is all we have. But I would like you to take a look at it, and I will ask you just a few questions about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, does that video, at least those portions that we were able to see, accurately reflect part of the discussion at the press conference on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall General Forand talking about the UN troops being able to hold back the HV in certain portions?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recalled some of what he said now, now that have I seen it again, that he said the very initial phases of the operation. That was the Zone of Separation and the UN in the Zone of Separation largely he was referring to, and that was quite a big concern for the General in terms of what was going on to the UN peacekeepers in the Zone of Separation in the four battalion areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That press conference took place in the ARSK army headquarters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. We went to the government building where the press centre usually was at the back as a separate room but I think everything in basic chaos. We found ourselves I think in the ante-room to the canteen/cafeteria area that is in the central lobby or was in the central lobby of that main building downstairs. You can see the boarded up background and everything. Yeah. It was have very impromptu press briefing bearing in mind the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were there armed ARSK soldiers in the vicinity of the place that you were holding your press conference?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. Everything was very much fluid. It was not a very long press briefing, but I don't recall that there were military people running around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we show the video one more time. If you could now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, could you assist me. This video was not shown to General Forand?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We received the video within the last three days, Your Honour. So I didn't have it at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that explains, because my question would have been it would not have been put to Mr. Forand. But please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you could pay attention in the background there and see if you can spot anyone with a weapon in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go back a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is that person carrying a rifle in the back? It's a shadowy figure, but do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coming in now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right above General Forand's head there. There seems to be a rifle or something there off to the left of the individual. Directly under the letter K if you --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking. I in honesty can't be sure. I don't know what people are seeing at the same time that I'm looking at this. But I can't recall from looking at it that it is, but you may have analysed it better than me. I don't know. I didn't, from where I'm seated down on the seat there, see anything behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just looking at the same as all of us are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I thought maybe that would refresh your recollection. Your Honour, I would tender the video then into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, no objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit D703, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D703 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, let me show you a few documents and, again, this is in the interests of saving some time. I will show you about three documents and then ask you a few questions about it. Before I do, on that video did you recognise who your interpreter was there?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is the interpreter I referred to yesterday in our session, in the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could call up 1D41-0024.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the security department of the command of the 7th corps of the ARSK. Topic is Alun Roberts, spokesman, Sector South command observations. And then the first paragraph says: The security department of the military department --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether we should go into private session for this. I can explain it briefly why I think it might be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, let me say that we are now going to look through a series of documents seized by the Croatian government from ARSK intelligence services. This is in line with operation Horizont, which we looked at yesterday towards the end of the day. If names appear in these documents, you should be aware that that does not mean that the -- that the Trial Chamber has made a finding that the individuals referenced there actually engaged in the activities referenced in the documents. That will be a decision for the Trial Chamber to make at a later date. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Reliability of these documents is a matter still to be considered, but these documents apparently exist. And they -- Mr. Misetic will put some questions about. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, the document we have on the screen, Mr. Roberts, references you at the top, the date is 14 December 1994. And it says: "The security department of the military department, through the cooperation with Agent Student, obtained certain materials regarding Rob Henderson --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Information, it reads, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Certain information Rob Henderson, a Canadian, as well as materials, photocopied materials) that he found on Alun Roberts's table." And the bottom paragraph notes what the attachment is, which were documents found on Alun Roberts's table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could -- again, I'm going group these together so if I could tender this into evidence and get a D number for it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D704.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D704 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have 1D41-0032, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the 24th of November, 1994. The subject is Kotil, Roberts, Stigner. I don't know if I pronounced that correctly. "Observation of their activities and then again the document references the contact with the Agent Student, expanded its knowledge of activities of Kotil, Roberts, and Stigner and other members of the UNPROFOR in the newly emerged situation." If you go down to the fourth paragraph: "Alongside other materials the agent submitted a letter sent by General Kotil to General Ante Gotovina commending the latter for his cooperation in solving the problem of the observation post in Crno by Zadar. "The agent was instructed to continue his activities and to report on significant events." Can we turn the page to this document, please?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to the end of the document, scroll up. Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Tell us when you're ready, Mr. Roberts.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I was waiting for you --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The work method applied," on the bottom, "the object of the method of application, Kotil, Roberts and Stigner." If we could go to the next page, please. These are the actual notes of the meeting with Agent Student. You can take a look at it, if you wish. Talks about where you live, what you're doing. I won't read it. I'll let you take a look. Tell me when you're finished, Mr. Roberts.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit number D705, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D705 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have 1D41-0040, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, I can imagine that you'd like to -- I don't whether you can store all the information because the questions are postponed until after we've seen all the documents. If there would be any need for you to look at the documents, again I take it that there are hard copies available. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This a document 20 November 1994. Cover sheet mentions again the meeting with Agent Student regarding the meeting between the commander of the 7th Corps and HV General Gotovina which was also attended by the commander of Sector South. Cover page asks or says that the agent, meaning Agent Student was instructed to monitor the activities of UNPROFOR and any indicators of possible Ustasha aggression against the RSK. If we could go to the third page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me read the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Again just tell me when you're finished.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the third page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: These are the actual explanation or notes of the meeting with Agent Student. Second paragraph: "On 18 November 1994, I held a special meeting with Agent Student, due to the fact that we needed to urgently investigate an important document. "At the aforementioned meeting which was held in Zemunik, our agent arrived with Alun Roberts." Now first let me just ask you, Zemunik, just for the Trial Chamber, was in Croatian-held territory. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zemunik was the crossing point -- one of the crossing points that was an official crossing point between the internal sector to go across the Zone of Separation to what we can say is -- was then Croatian territory proper and proceed on to various cities, towns in Croatia proper at that time. You come back through that if you're going into Zadar, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you read the rest of the paragraph but just I will read out the fourth paragraph: "Our agent wasn't able to hear the separate conversation between General Kotil and General Gotovina because he was, most of the time, at the side of Alun Robertson," should be Alun Roberts, "as his interpreter." Then it says: "Upon returning from Zemunik to Knin our agent was able to take off from the fax machine at the southern camp the letter of De Laprel for President Martic." Tell me when you're finished reading the document, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just for the Court Chamber, I think either you, sir, or me should make maybe some references to who these other people are and the fact that they are UN personnel that are referred to in various places there in the last paragraph, not that they're international organisations. They're UN officials. Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Roberts, I'll stop here and ask you some questions. Were you aware that you were attending official meetings with interpreters who were in fact agents, intelligence agents of the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I ask that in order to give a full reply we go into private session or -- I'm in the hands of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to refer to names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we turn into private session in which you can explain why you consider it necessary to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, first may I -- am I allowed to put to the witness what he has just said in terms of the conversation that was described?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd briefly summarize that and in as neutral wording as possible, then there's no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, I think while we were in private session you said that the Agent Student, you believe to be an individual named Predrag Sare and that Mr. Sare at some point advised you and other members of the UN in Sector South that he in fact was being pressured to provide intelligence -- pressured by the Serb authorities to provide intelligence information to their intelligence services. Have I accurately summarized what you have stated? And if I haven't, please clarify.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can go into this -- I'm also aware that we're in open session and that we're now going to say about this person, I'm clearly sure is going to jeopardize not just reputation, but future activities in a very definite sense, but if that's on the record and I'm advised I must reply, then, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course the Chamber will also consider justified concerns for the safety and security of witnesses. We have protective measures for that. However, in the present situation we're now talking about, apparently, of course, we would have to hear all of the evidence, but apparently not talking about people's -- people being victimised and people being exposed to threats or threats against the welfare of themselves or their families because they testify, but for totally different reasons, the Chamber, at this moment, sees no reason to specifically protect the persons in relation to which questions will be put. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person named as the interpreter, Mr. Sare, as I said in answer to the question, yes, he had come to the UN and confessed these so-called pressures that he was passing information to the authorities in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So would it fair to say then -- first can you give us a date. When did he have this conversation with you?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about this time, as far as I can recall. It was not only with me. I think that it was also prior to that with other UN officials in Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So when you "this time," you're referring to November and December 1994?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be exact. I'm just looking at the dates of this correspondence and the activities of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, winter of 1994?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately like that, yes. It was towards the end of that year, maybe something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, yesterday we went through the UN peacekeeping manual for public information. One of the rules was UN needs to maintain impartiality particularly with its local staff, yet you after being advised by Mr. Sare in the winter of 1994 that he was being pressured to and in fact had passed information to RSK intelligence, you continued to employ him as your interpreter, including at official meetings with General Gotovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I, first of all, do not employ, as I understand the crux of your question, recruit or employ people. That's the UN personnel's department. He was not an interpreter specifically for the press office. I explained he was also a -- an interpreter, sorry, for the other departments of the UN in Sector South, the civil affairs department, humanitarian department and occasionally for the sector commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between question and answer, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You utilized him as your interpreter even -- oh, sorry. Even after you found out that he was passing information, you personally continued to utilize him as your interpreter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used him on occasions, but I also more frequently used other interpreters who were available to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And could I add on that same point, that I understand the thrust of this is being put to me as the public information officer. Again, this was discussed by senior officials in headquarters Sector South outside of my knowledge, and he continued as an interpreter on the role of the interpreter's pool in Sector South headquarters at that time, attending not only information meetings but also was thought okay to attend political meetings with the RSK authorities on UN matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Roberts --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First can I tender this document. In light of this question, I have to move on to a separate document to show the witness, but I tender this document into evidence that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit number D706, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D706 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, let me take you to 65 ter 4044. This is a document tendered by the Prosecution into evidence. You will recognise this report. This is the report of 9 August 1995 in which you, amongst other things, in great detail describe the incident with the interpreter when he went back to his apartment. Now if we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, the date, as a matter of fact, I don't know whether it has been an attempt to highlight by a marker or something like that, but the date --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand corner, Your Honour, and it has been produced by the Prosecution as having been written on the 9th of August, but in the upper right-hand corner there's a fax date of 9 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I don't think it is an exhibit yet. It is it part of our motion to admit it via this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just said it was tendered. I know it's awaiting whether it is going to be admitted or not, but ... on the second page, Your Honour, you can also see the fax line, and the incident itself, I believe occurred on the 9th of August so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Just for us -- just for you to know that we have difficulties in reading what appears after Wednesday and of course we may have other -- the problem is that as far as the fax is concerned, that not the whole of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next page has the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now you're writing this memo to Filip Arnold, who is the UNCRO/UNPROFOR spokesman in Zagreb, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief spokesperson in the nation at the time of Operation Storm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And when you're righting this, you're aware that part of the purpose of writing this to Mr. Arnold as the spokesman is so that he can, if necessary, put this information out into the international community. Correct.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not the precise purpose. Otherwise, I would have suggested a press line for that particular thing, which was the normal practice if I was suggesting an incident deserved comment by the chief spokesperson at the press briefing. I would usually suggest a press line and they would take it or not. This was just to -- essentially to inform of what had happened on that particular day. There was a separate report sent, by the way, from the civil affairs office to, I think the SRSG.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could look at paragraph 8. "On first time visits to Knin yesterday, local Serb interpreters who accompanied UN personnel reported being intimidated. The worst example was that of a long-time and distinguished civil affairs interpreter." Now, you're writing to Mr. Arnold approximately eight months after you discovered that Mr. Sare is passing information, whether under pressure or not, and you write to Mr. Arnold and describe him as a long-time and distinguished civil affairs interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you think that was a full and complete description to Mr. Arnold of what the situation really was?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now for some background information, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me take the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did ask me a question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I think the witness may --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- answer the question if he thinks that some background information would clarify the matter. Mr. Roberts, could you try to be brief as to the background and focus on the foreground.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In reference to the word "distinguished civil affairs interpreter," and long-time, he had been there since, I think, the early part of the mission, 1992/1993 in various periods. I know he had been assaulted by elements of the so-called RSK paramilitary on one occasion with me and other UN personnel. We were hijacked at gunpoint by unknown but believed to be with RSK paramilitary vehicle stolen and assaulted and had also been in areas near the front line in very difficult and dangerous situations before the cease-fire agreement. So that's in there for background reference. And we can now continue. That's the background. The Court can take it for its own consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now the question, because you gave a bit of the background -- the question was whether you thought that this was a full and complete description to Mr. Arnold of what the situation really was. You have emphasised, apparently, the difficulties the interpreter had undergone, but that was not the gist of the question by Mr. Misetic and you have made note of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question simply is wouldn't it not have been appropriate to describe him in other terms as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, I accept that. At the time I thought it was not inappropriate from the situation to use those words, and in reference to the actual confession if that had been passed on to the then chief spokesperson prior to Mr. Arnold.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question is you could have limited yourself also to an interpreter, which would have not be -- which would not have been very complete information but, at the same time, it would not have -- unbalanced information you just referred to his work, his job.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have actually more concerns than simply in addition to how you described them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It goes what you're actually describing happened. If we could go to paragraph 13. Now, you have already described in prior paragraphs the tense situation. You say: "One of the soldiers," meaning HV "then went back into the building. A short time later he emerged with a paper. This was pushed in PIO's face and told, in so many words, this has RSK army stamp. This man's name, he is war crime, you give now." If we go to the next page, which is the second portion of paragraph 16. It would appear that Mr. Sare had in fact taken something out of the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll up the English page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in the middle there of that top paragraph: "In addition, photographs were removed from his possessions, one with his brother years ago, showing two young men in plain green uniform dress." Now, Mr. Roberts, I put it to you that Predrag Sare went back to his apartment to get documents out of his apartment before the HV arrived. Isn't that what really happened?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went back to inspect the accommodation of several staff and we were with the interpreter, myself and another UN international employee, and he was in the apartment very briefly and we were with him, and it was basically, as far as we could see, an inspection of what was already a looted apartment with possessions and objects strewn around, and I can't be clear that in the time we had before Croatian soldiers came in and intervened and seemed to know who he was, that this assault situation began. I'm pretty sure we did not leave him alone to collect or get things from any drawers. We were all there in the apartment together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I turn your attention then to paragraph 9 of your own report on the screen, which is page 2 of this document. Paragraph 9: "As the PIO and civil affairs officer left the apartment block with the interpreter still inside, they were challenged in a very threatening manner on why they were there." So apparently, sir, there was a time when you left the apartment and left Predrag in the apartment by himself. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had gone down the stairs and he was still inside the apartment block but not far behind us. I don't think we had left him at all in the apartment on his own. It was then that we were challenged by the Croatian soldiers as they came in, but, at that time, I don't think the interpreter was still left alone sorting things in the apartment. We had come down together but we were ahead of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if you left the apartment block, you left him inside --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is an interpretation here, I think, in terms of inside the apartment itself and inside the apartment block, and I have said as we came out of the apartment block I recall we had gone down ahead. So, yes, for a moment or two he was behind us and still in the actual apartment itself as we had gone down maybe two flights of stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, you know that Predrag Sare went into that apartment looking to retrieve documents before the HV arrived. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know that, and the observation of myself and the other international interpreter was that it was found to be in a complete disarray and a mess. I don't recall that he had time or sufficient opportunity to really go through things or conceal that he was obtaining information or documents from us. We were still inside the actual apartment itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, we've already noted that you said a photograph was removed from his possession, a photograph was one with his brother years ago showing two young men in plain green uniform dress? Who is Predrag Sare's brother?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I didn't meet his brother. I know his brother was something in terms of a -- a special unit. That's about all I know and I know that as far as family went, from what I was told and understood, they were not close but that's for the -- for consideration. But I know that he had photographs of all his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You know they were twins. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they were, but I don't think that it was something that was known to me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You also are very well aware, Mr. Roberts, that Predrag Sare's twin brother Nenad was one of Milosevic's assassins. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of Milosevic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at that. I'm surprised that --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're saying Mr. Milosevic -- I think you mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please clarify what you mean by Milosevic assassins.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps also the relevancy of this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's relevant. There is an issue of bias that the witness has put forward that this individual was doing things unwillingly because of threats by RSK personnel and I'm going to go into this person's connection with certain high levels in addition to his connection as an interpreter for other high-level Serbian officials --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me show you 1D41-0345. This is an Agence France-Presse article of September 22nd, 2004, describing the trial of Milorad Ulemovic [phoen] Legija in Belgrade for the assassination of Serbian ex-president Ivan Stambolic. You will note in paragraph 2 Judge Dragoljub Albijanic said protected witness Nenad Sare will testify in camera in the proceedings resumed in a high-security court for organised crime. "A former secret police agent, Sare has reportedly confessed to participating in the operation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, of course, everything comes as entirely new to us. Apparently from this newspaper article it appears that testimony has been given in camera. Now it is known to many judges in this Tribunal that sometimes secrets are published in newspapers despite orders not to publish matters. I'm not aware of whether what follows in this is in violation of any order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honour, and as an officer of the Court I can tell that you I have researched the issue and Serbian authority have very much emphasised Nenad Sare because he is the person who actually led them to the body of Ivan Stambolic, and so it's not a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to make sure that not only in this courtroom where confidentiality is treated as an important matter, that in this same courtroom we would violate confidentiality rules. I have not researched the background. I then rely upon you as an officer of the court not to make any mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Sare has reportedly confessed to participating in the operation to kidnap and murder Stambolic, the president of the Balkan republic from 1986 to 19887. "He led police to a mountain north of Belgrade where Stambolic's remains were found last year, almost four years after the former president disappeared from a park in the Serbian capital." Let me show you several exhibits again and then we can ask some questions. Your Honour, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I doubt the relevancy but I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D707, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D707 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could now call up 1D41-0060.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, of course, this whole matter, I do understand that you're challenging the reliability and credibility of this witness. That may not come as a surprise to Mr. Roberts either. Of course, to highlight the whole background is -- could be relevant. At the same time, of course, the first issue or the last issue would be to what extent the witness was aware of these kind of things, and if just to highlight all of this and then to, at the end, find out that the witness was not aware, that of course doesn't make much sense because then it might still be relevant but not in relation to this witness, who may have been, I'm not saying he was, but may have been mislead about matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But it's not only bias and credibility of this witness. Your Honour, I will to address that concern move from this document right to the next document to show you what the other issue is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Then I will go very quickly through this -- not even through this. If you can take a look at it quickly, Mr. Roberts, but essentially at the bottom of this page, talks about Ulemek passing an order to a criminal group consisting of state officials with the JSO, identifies the people and the next page says accomplice Nenad Sare. Rather than take more time on it then, Your Honour, I will tender that into evidence and proceed to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit D708, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D708 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I may have 1D41-0376, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is HRAT compilation of statements taken from witnesses in the camp. Now, Mr. Roberts, you testified earlier this week that part of your own reports were based on UN CIVPOL reports of interviews taken with some of the people in the camp. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I would ask you to -- if I could just ask the registrar to flip through every page of these statements perhaps we could not publish it so that the witness's names don't appear. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document, the following page is not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the documents later to be tendered under seal as a whole, although the first page doesn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- harm. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could flip through every page and note who the interpreter is for these witness statements. I don't know how far along we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But I think, Mr. Roberts, you understand the point. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the point, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I tender the document into evidence, Your Honours, for the purpose of showing Mr. Sare's involvement in the drafting of the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps also to -- of course we could read that but I thought that except for three --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask him some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D709, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D709 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First again as a background question so I don't have to go through it, when Mr. Sare was confessing his passing information, did he also acknowledge to you that he been General Ratko Mladic's interpreter in the early part of the war?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was not only known to me but to other senior members of the UN before I even came to Sector South. I recall being told that not by the person concerned but I think by people from Sector South -- Sector South commander's office when I arrived there, that he had -- he worked there and I think that is on his employment application or CV, submitted by him to the UN in terms of him being an interpreter at the headquarters of the government building in the -- in the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. EJ Flynn, Ms. Grace Kang, some of these other people that worked for HRAT, they came into the theatre in August, and my question to you is did you advise them that the interpreter that they were working with had, A, told you that he had previously been passing information to the Serb authorities; and B, was the former translator for General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had advised them -- I'm not sure Grace, but I advised EJ in terms of the background to the whole thing in terms of confession, the UN decision, which was not mine, but personnel that this was known and he was continued in employment of the UN after the time he made that statement to the UN officials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was twofold.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did brief them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you paid attention only to could I say the confession and not to the previous position as Mr. Mladic's interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that I explained the whole thing of the most important thing for me was to brief in terms of the UN --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What is important you informed them about the first issue and not about the second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me take you to two additional points before the break. Your 1997 statement, P675, paragraph 42. This is now discussing the alleged threat by General Gotovina against you. And it says: "UN officials that he wanted General Forand to know that, inter alia, we consider Alun Roberts as a spy and that regardless of what he is doing, if he is seen on the streets, he could be eliminated, his further safety cannot be guaranteed ... General Forand told me later that in his mind, he could not be sure but it seemed a clear threat." And if we could pull up, please, 1D41-0367. This is a -- this is a handwritten diary provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by an ECMM official named Soren Liborius. Do you recall Mr. Liborius?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We received this over the weekend, Your Honour, so we're not able, I don't believe to do a B/C/S translation. But I will read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is Mr. Laborious's entry from 6 September which, is the day after the meeting between General Forand and General Gotovina, and he says: "Meet General Gotovina, sector commander, 5 September 1995. General Got," which I assume is Gotovina, "PIO accused of spying, disinformation and sufficient for a case in court. PIO, Gotovina very emotional during meeting." My question to you is, "the PIO:" At the bottom to me would indicate that this is a conversation or information that is being passed to Mr. Liborius from you, and in your own 1997 statement you make reference to the fact that General Forand said he could not be sure. My question to you is do you recall having a conversation with Soren Liborius on the 6th, where what you said was that Gotovina had accused you of spying and disinformation and that there was sufficient evidence for a case in court against you?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not recognise this at all as my note, at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is not said that this was your note, but that since PIO appears on the fourth line as perhaps the source of what Mr. Liborius did write down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. I did not recall at all having a meeting with ECMM, Mr. Liborius on the 6th of September, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the document into evidence and I think it is a good time for a break as I will be shifting subjects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections and Mr. Liborius will come to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D710.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D710 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Misetic, could you give us an impression on how long you're two hours are --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Two hours and 55 minutes left, but I will try to finish by -- sorry, Your Honour. I will try to finish by the second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Waespi, would that be sufficient for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So far I need about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About ten minutes. Then we will have a break, and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I again have to apologise on behalf of the Chamber for the late start. Mr. Misetic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, let's turn our attention to the 4th of August, 1995. And you have given some testimony here about what you observed on the morning of the 4th. Now, is it fair to say that your observations consist of what you saw on the balcony of your apartment in the morning of the 4th as well as what you saw on the balcony of UN headquarters when you arrived in Sector South headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fair assessment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now I note in your 7 February 2008 statement at page 3, paragraph 8 you say, I was on the balcony for about ten minutes. Is that accurate? Sorry. Just to be accurate, when I say balcony, I meant the balcony of your apartment.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ten minutes at one particular time, not just for only one occasion only for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How much time in total did you spend on the balcony of your apartment on the morning of the 4th?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To describe it, maybe three or four occasions very briefly, and one occasion, maybe four or five minutes, and one occasion, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You state in 1998, page 4, that from your observations you concluded that about 200 civilian locations were hit during the shelling which included roofs that were damaged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You say in 2007 at page 5 at 28 February 2007, in later weeks this was confirmed by my regular journeys into town where I could see damage to the rooftops of what were civilian buildings in several different parts of the town. None of these buildings were near RSK government, military, or police locations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ask am I supposed to be seeing on the screen here the statement or not, because I'm not seeing anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It could be shown to you or a hard copy could be given to the witness if there's one available. But perhaps as we could -- as soon as Mr. Misetic gives the P number, then the registrar usually shows it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: P677. Page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At the top of the page. Do you see that sentence: "In later weeks this was confirmed."

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting the top paragraph, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is right in the middle of that top, continued paragraph from the previous page right in the middle there's a sentence that starts: "In later weeks this was confirmed by my regular journeys ..."

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In later weeks, driving around town, yeah, in -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we call up Exhibit D276, please. Oh, yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a video, a panoramic. You will see a video from 5 August 1995. And I'd ask you to take a look at the video and point out where the roof damage was the greatest in your trips out of Knin in the weeks after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we haven't got the whole of Knin there by any means. But buildings in the centre of town, I have provided a sketch map of buildings I saw hit. Apartment blocks to the centre, I mean, I can't with this photograph here pick out a broad dimension of Knin. It would have to be more detailed than that in terms of streets and so on. If that's possible, I don't know, but can I point out on here what I saw that are not, to my mind, military buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you see any of the buildings in the areas that are depicted in this video?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Behind the -- the gentleman, there are houses on a dirt road that were hit. They were buildings on the roads that were going down from the top of the fortress that were civilian that I saw hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm pausing because of the interpreters. Are you saying that you saw them in the video or are you saying you saw them even though they're not in the video?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought the question was in your trips around town later weeks, you suggest or point out from this video the apartment buildings or the areas mainly that you saw hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Then so, first, let me ask you, did you see any of those buildings in this video?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rough general areas, yes, can I say that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it has to go more slowly I think in terms of that, and this is with all fairness a portion of the town and quite a short video-clip, but I -- run it again, perhaps, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What we'll do is we'll run the video and we'll pause it in the various sections of town as they come on the screen, and then you can tell us roughly where you believe there was roof damage.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, down from the [indiscernible] there is a dirt road running down here and off camera. Houses were hit --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher -- can he point on the video? No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But I think the cursor could be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- moved. That means no marking but -- and then of course for the record we have to describe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what we see now is the dirt road that's described by the witness below the wall not visible on this video image. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you would have to move the -- this frame to the left so that the right-hand edge is further to show more, maybe, but you can't see down on that dirt road and on those houses which is just one section.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For the record, this is the still at 04 seconds on the video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is it behind -- well, along this street here this is behind the RSK buildings, but you have do go again at a different angle, but I pointed out one map, I think it is it to the -- beyond this building here, one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This building here, could you please tell us what this building here is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. To the left I think you go further left down that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you see the building now?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been more precise on an aerial shot that was shown earlier, but there is a building in this row was hit by the side shelling but I can't pick it out of your -- on this, whether it is the actual real street. We did this with the investigation of a quite wider shot of the centre part of town and picked out that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you say "this row of buildings," you're referring to what apparently is a street going from the left side at approximately 50 per cent of the eighth of the picture to the right side approximately 30 per cent of the eighth of the picture. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is but I don't think it is possible to pull back so that you can get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. This is video images which are not -- cannot be manipulated at this moment. We can follow it, we can look at it, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my mind if we're pointing, this building here appears to be the same one that I've marked on the specific map exhibit given to the -- to the statement, but I'm not exactly sure this is the precise one because I need to see the whole length of this area. But it's of this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is that the building that you're pointing to?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm pointing along here. I'm saying in all honesty, looking at the video-clip, I apologise, but I don't think it is possible to pick out precisely that this was the building. I have been quite I think specific on in the earlier exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is -- I'm afraid that one has to review -- no, the problem is that the cursor is not part of the evidence; it's just the description. The witness started pointing at a building, which is in the left lower corner of what seems to be a sports complex but then opposite side of the road with a white element in the roof structure, then moved a little bit to the right bottom direction where a structure can be seen in the midst of some green, and then moved a little bit further up higher to the right, where do I say, series of roofs which are not very good visible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. And for the record this is at the 15-second still on this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Misetic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to say this is possible but this is showing a fragment of Knin in the centre from the very high-up elevation of the castle and -- Well, you can't see it again, I'm afraid, but if you go behind these buildings where I'm pointing with my finger, if the cursor can come up, and again, I have seen other, forgive me, better aerial views of Knin, and I'm not wanting, Your Honour, in any way to go and put my finger on an area which puts like three rooftops in question when we're trying to be quite careful in saying, Well, this was three rooftops I saw together, that is not exact, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness now with the cursor pointed at the whitish --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is pointed at a roof but I'm looking at the actual gap between the roof and a street area which we can't see on this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, if you have difficulties in identifying the roofs, then please tell us, if these were -- is one of the areas where the roofs were damaged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have to look left to get a better bearing, if that is the street concerned that I'm interested in. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me play it and see if it goes farther left. This is, by the way, for the record this conversation took place at the 19-second mark of this video. Does that assist you, Mr. Roberts? We're now at the 20-second mark on the video.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, a little bit. Judging by the edge of the fortress, it's buildings, if I recall, through this gap here that, again, are blocked by this building here further down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say, for the record, I'm sorry, Your Honour, but we're talking about a very important issue, obviously. We're looking down from a very steep elevation, and only when you're travelling up or going from street to street are you going to be able to sort of spot on a proper way tops of buildings or damage to the side that can you see that I don't, in all honesty, believe that you can depict from this kind of video, and that's not trying to avert -- and we're in the centre of Knin as well, which was the main focus, I know, of a lot of media and a lot of attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, is it fair to say that based on this video you can't by looking at this video identify any specific buildings that were hit by shelling -- roofs, I should say that you were hit by shelling?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give general areas, but I'm not a hundred percent sure that they really would be in those areas or the buildings concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that is now -- I mean the purpose of this exercise is whether the pictures support your statement about what areas you found damage to roofs, and now to say, I could indicate the areas on the basis of these pictures, not by pointing at roof damage but just as the areas doesn't add anything to the testimony or to the statement given by the witness. So, I think that's a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. We'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your statements you said that your conclusions on the shelling were based also on information that you received from other UN sources. And at your 1998 statement, which is P676 at page 5 you say, at the very top of the page, fifth line down: "About an hour later, when I called back to the UNMO office, two of the duty officers said that from their assessment of the bombardment that hit Knin they assessed that between around 0500 hours and about 0800 hours, around 1100 shells had targeted Knin." Do you recall the names of the two UNMO officers who gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, no, recall those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can I call up exhibit P101, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is an UNMO report filed by UNMO HQ Sector South on 4 August at 1205. It says in the very first paragraph: "HV shelling on Knin started at 0500 Bravo, August, and continued up to 1040 Bravo, August 1995. Total around 350 to 400 artillery MBRL rocket fire were heard by the UNMOs in Knin." Did you receive this report as part of your duties on the day of 4 August 1995 as the PIO who was communicating with the international press?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen this document, and my response on seeing this was to go back to ask what it meant on the third line down there: "Total around 350 to 400 RT/MRBL/rocket fire were heard by the UNMOs in Knin," and I wanted to know that in terms of, okay, we've had a conversation a large number of assessment had been told me, are we talking about hearing or seeing or generalist estimation, but this was sent as the position of hearing what was the position of UNMOs in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So was it based on the fact that you received on a regular basis UNMO reports, was it standard for UNMO to report something like having heard shell fire but leave out of an UNMO report the fact that they had seen -- seen several hundred more artillery impacts in town? Would that have been common practice by UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would go -- no, no it's not. I would go always by what is written on paper, even if someone told me, Alun, to the best of my ability, it's that number. In the early hours as you said I was in touch with international press once I got into HQ Sector South which was not for some time after the bombardment began. I did not pass on to press anything in terms of numbers, because everything was very, as I said in my statement, very fluid and I don't think I'm on record myself of going and giving a number of X shells, buildings, everything on the 4th of August. Others, I think may have done, but not from myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it possible, sir, that the number you gave in the witness statement of 1100 shells came from -- that number came to you from Andrew Leslie and not UNMO?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't from Mr. Leslie. I definitely went down to the UNMO office downstairs from the second floor, which was inside and right -- and I was frequently in there because they had very good maps of the entire sector and enlarged maps of cities along the whole of the Sector South and the hinterland of Croatia. So that's the point I wanted to go and see, and also because I felt, Okay, UNMOs are able to give a good assessment in terms of detonations, artillery, and that's where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, taking you to your February 7, 2008 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, if we could pull that up, which is P678, please, at page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There you say in the middle of paragraph 33 that an as PIO you "especially regarded UNMO reports in Sector South as being particularly accurate for the reason that they were compiled by experts in military ordnance." Is that accurate, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my general feeling of UNMOs in not only that situation but, in general, of what expertise was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, I believe, and I'm looking for the reference here, but you said in your witness statement of 28 February 2007 that, A report had been prepared by senior UNMO, which would have been passed to UNPROFOR HQ on the damage caused by shell fire in Knin. Do you recall any such report?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recall that that's -- a report -- sorry. A report was made by UNMOs and passed to headquarters on an assessment of, I think, shell damage, and there were other reports on general assessment of buildings as well in Knin and other places, also by -- headquarters. There were several UNMO reports prepared and sent to headquarters assessing damage, some by the various teams collectively and one, I think, particularly looked at Knin in three or four different parts of Knin, looking at damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can I have the registrar please put up Exhibit P64, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is an UNMO report on the shelling prepared on 18 August 1995 by UNMO H -- SMO, Sector South. SMO, you'll recall was Steiner Hjertnes?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall having seen this report as part of your responsibilities as the PIO?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw this report but this, I recall is not the only UNMO report I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you will note then you saw this report.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This report at paragraph 2, concludes: "In general shelling was concentrated against military objectives. The damages caused by shelling to civilian establishments is concentrated to the close vicinity of military objectives. Only few, three to five impacts is observed in other urban areas."

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When you saw this report did that -- and it was a report by people whom you now in court confirm to be particularly accurate for the reason that these reports were compiled by experts in military ordnance. When you received that report, did that impact the conclusion which you've given to this Trial Chamber in the witness statements that the shelling was indiscriminate, it was hitting civilian areas, and that civilian buildings had been hit?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Can I take you through this, two, three, paragraphs. My impression when I got this and I think we're talking about the 18th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Provisional assessment damage caused by HV ops 4 to 6 August 1995 at Knin. Provisional assessment by Podgonja [phoen] team, a rundown, is based on a rundown of 70 per cent of Knin town and gives only a brief -- a brief overview of the situation. Correct? In general, shelling was -- right. Right. I recall when I had this of being quite surprised. It is not my place as the press officer to go and try and challenge or change a report. But between the 6th of August and the date of this report that I saw on that day, there had been several discussions between sector commander's office and UNMOs in regard to damage, and I felt those discussions were characterized in other reports that had gone to headquarters mission of a larger extent of damage. And I think there were -- there are reports that exist prior to this and after that give a different picture. I don't think this is the only and final one, but I have seen this report, I do see what it says, and the reason -- the reason I'm saying is that I know there were statements made, including by the sector commander, to the press from the press office phone giving his perspective of information in based upon UNMOs and collaboration with his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say you don't have any particular military expertise to analyse shelling damage?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any professional expertise to assess, and what you have said, I would agree with and I would add a "but." The "but" is well into the end of August, I, with one other UNMO, went out into Knin. I did not stay with him but he was going to make an assessment of detailed and minor damage to get an impression towards that part of late August. As far as I know, that was done. I don't know if that was passed as a general UNMO survey but that was looking at buildings around the town and I, again, driving around, was picking out not vast devastation of rooftops but clear signs that rooftops were hit and that I felt was in later report of UNMOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What was the name of that UNMO?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You referenced --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a Norwegian or a Dutch UNMO that went out. There was an issue which we had recurring of a lack of photographic equipment at the time of all this happening. Sorry. I'm drawing attention here to your second paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and the surprise was only few, (3 to five impacts) is observed in other urban areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question on the basis of your last answer. We've seen extensive pictures from you. You testified that you were the only one that had a United Nations camera. Why didn't you take pictures of 200 houses with shell damage?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a good question. Part of the time we were out in the streets and there was still signs of Croatian soldiers. That was one reason why not. Later, it was possible, and I did not do it. The other thing we had a problem with, it is not important, but we did not have vast amounts of film roll or access to film roll in our office or from mission headquarters. This was a place you could not go out to, as background, into Knin and buy 12 rounds of video film or still film for the camera. It was limited and we were using extensively this, as things went on, for photographs not just by me but by colleagues of the Human Rights Action Team in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, I am quite sure that you are aware that the issue of the shelling of Knin was of high international awareness as early as the 4th of August, 1995, that the allegation was in the international community and not something that was simply an allegation in Sector South headquarters, and I put it to you, given the amount of attention in the international press to the alleged indiscriminate shelling of Knin, are you telling us that you actually found evidence of this, saw it with your own eyes but decided you weren't going to take pictures because you didn't want to waste film? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: We have seen photographs that were taken by Mr. Roberts that show shelling damages. There are at least two we have seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, I think that -- I would leave it to counsel to -- to speak without asking prior permission. The words by both the accused are not translated, but I -- if there's any reason for an accused to speak aloud, then, of course, through counsel, you may ask permission to do so. Then going back, Mr. Waespi, I'm reading, again ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It is P683.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But it is not part of the question. You can object against the question, but Mr. Misetic sought confirmation of how he understood the testimony and that is not directly related to whatever we've seen at that moment. He is asking without -- without including in his question that in no way ever a roof has been hit by a shell. That was not the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
